title: A mean extent shift matched 77% of Antarctic 10 million km2 season shortening in 2016-2024
abstract: We tested how much Antarctic season shortening can follow from a lower extent curve with the same seasonal shape. We used Sea Ice Index Version 4 daily values for 36 March-to-February seasons. Relative to 1989-2015, the season above 10 million km2 was 15.37 days shorter in 2016-2024. A fixed daily template shifted by each season mean gave 11.81 days of shortening, or 77% of the observed change. The remaining shortening was 3.56 days, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of 1.33 to 5.67 days. The template was rebuilt in each resample. The residual interval included zero at thresholds of 8 and 14 million km2. Most of the main timing change can thus follow from a mean level change without a change in seasonal shape. A smaller shape difference remains at the main threshold. This is a retrospective geometric test, not a forecast or physical attribution. One product, selected periods and thresholds, nine recent seasons and dependence assumptions limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, a figure and a separate crossing audit are included. Source and annual records remain external.
